recentItems.title: Breaking News LIVE: Secret Service Escorts Trump Out of Press Conference | World News LIVE
recentItems.description:
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump was abruptly escorted from the White House press briefing room by a Secret Service agent on Monday evening following a shooting incident just outside the complex. Trump returned to the podium approximately nine minutes later to explain that a suspect had been shot by law enforcement near the White House fence on 17th Street and Pennsylvania Avenue. According to the Secret Service, a 51-year-old male suspect approached an officer, claimed to have a weapon, and moved aggressively before being shot and hospitalized. The White House complex was not breached, and officials confirmed that no protectees were in danger during the incident.

recentItems.title: West Bank Shooting: Netanyahu Orders Hebron Sealed, Full West Bank Closure After Attack | Watch
recentItems.description:
Five people were wounded, two seriously, in a shooting near Yehuda Junction in the Hebron area, according to the provided report. The IDF said two attackers were killed as troops launched searches and established roadblocks. The incident comes amid heightened Israeli security preparations ahead of the October 27 election, with officials warning of potential threats from Hamas and Iran-backed groups. Authorities have not established whether the shooting was linked to the election-related warnings.
.

recentItems.title: Elon Musk's $445 MN Political Spending Pushes To Boost Republicans Ahead Of US Midterms 2026
recentItems.description:
Elon Musk has poured more than $445 million into the 2026 US midterm elections, backing Republicans as they fight to retain control of the Senate and House. Federal Election Commission filings show fresh contributions to America PAC, alongside major donations to Republican-aligned groups. Musk’s political spending targets key congressional races through digital ads, text messages and voter outreach, raising questions about billionaire influence, campaign finance and the future of US politics.
